title: TRAI initiates phase-wise implementation of 1601-series for service and transactional calls by utilities, courier and logistics sectors entities
body_text:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today issued the Direction on use of 1601 series numbers for the transactional and service calls by the entities in sectors other than Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI) sector, and Government entities which are using numbers from 1600 series, issued earlier. Considering the critical and sensitive nature of communications made by the entities in BFSI sector and Government, this separate series has been issued for the sectors other than BFSI and Government in order to avoid mixing of important financial voice calls with the service and transactional calls from the other sectors.
After widespread adoption of the 1600-series numbers for service and transactional calls by BFSI sector entities, which has provided valuable experience for extending the trusted numbering framework to the other sectors also, TRAI has now initiated phase-wise implementation of the 1601-series allotted by the DoT for similar calls by the entities in sectors other than BFSI sector and Government. Based on consultations with stakeholders, it has been decided to implement the series, covering entities in Utilities, Courier and Logistics sectors under Phase-I .
The 1601-series numbers will be allocated directly to eligible entities, and not to intermediaries or aggregators, after due verification by the telecom service providers (TSPs).  Their adoption is, therefore, expected to become an important tool in combating impersonation by fraudsters who use normal 10-digit numbers and falsely claim to represent legitimate businesses. Moreover, the distinct numbering identity will enable the consumers to easily identify legitimate service and transactional calls, thereby, strengthening trust in such voice-based communications.
Key Provisions of the Direction
A. Phase-I sectors: The 1601-series shall be initially allocated to the eligible entities in the following sectors:
i. Utilities – Electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution companies, LPG distribution entities and such other utility service providers.
ii. Logistics and courier services – Courier companies, express logistics companies, parcel delivery service providers, freight and logistics service providers engaged in delivery of consignments.
B. Time-bound onboarding
The Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) have been asked to complete migration and onboarding of eligible entities covered under Phase-I within 90 days from the date of issue of the order.
C. Verification and exclusive use
The TSPs shall verify the eligibility of entities before assigning 1601-series numbers, and obtain an undertaking from them regarding exclusive use of these numbers for service and transactional voice calls. The numbers shall not be used for promotional voice calls by any entity.
*****
NJ/AR

enrichment.summary: TRAI has issued a Direction to implement the 1601-series of telephone numbers for service and transactional voice calls made by entities outside the BFSI and Government sectors, which already use the 1600-series. Phase-I of this rollout covers Utilities (electricity, water, gas, LPG distributors) and Logistics/Courier companies, with Telecom Service Providers required to complete verification and onboarding of eligible entities within 90 days. The numbers will be allotted directly to verified entities (not intermediaries) and can only be used for service/transactional calls, not promotional calls.
enrichment.context:
This move extends India's 'trusted numbering' framework, first introduced with the 1600-series for banks, financial institutions, and insurers, to combat rising instances of caller ID spoofing and fraud where scamsters impersonate legitimate businesses using ordinary 10-digit mobile numbers. With the growing volume of automated calls related to bill payments, OTPs, delivery updates, and service alerts from utilities and logistics companies, consumers have found it increasingly difficult to distinguish genuine calls from phishing attempts. By creating a distinct, verified numbering series exclusively for such purposes, TRAI aims to enhance consumer trust and provide an easy visual/audible cue for genuine communication.

This initiative is part of TRAI's broader regulatory push against unsolicited commercial communication and telecom fraud, which also includes measures like the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations (TCCCPR), mandatory registration of telemarketers, and blockchain-based scrubbing of promotional messages. The phased approach — starting with BFSI, then extending to Utilities and Logistics — reflects a calibrated, sector-wise rollout strategy that allows TRAI and TSPs to refine verification systems before wider adoption across other sectors like e-commerce, healthcare, and education.

prelims_questions.question: The '1601-series' of telephone numbers, recently notified by TRAI, is meant for which of the following purposes?
options: Service and transactional voice calls by Utilities and Logistics/Courier sector entities
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that TRAI has initiated the 1601-series for service and transactional calls by entities in sectors other than BFSI and Government, with Phase-I covering Utilities and Logistics/Courier sectors.

prelims_questions.question: Which regulatory body issued the Direction for phase-wise implementation of the 1601-series numbering system?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that TRAI issued the Direction, although the DoT had earlier allotted the number series.
